references.text: Deals with uncleanness after childbirth, which also lasts seven days, in the same way as the menstrual period in 15:19
Elaborates on the law concerning a woman's discharge of blood that continues beyond her normal menstrual period
Prohibits sexual intercourse with a woman during her menstrual period
Specifies the penalty for having sexual intercourse with a woman during her menstruation
Ezekiel uses menstrual uncleanness as a metaphor for Jerusalem's impurity
The prophet condemns those who have intercourse with women during their menstruation
The woman with a twelve-year discharge of blood touches Jesus, demonstrating his power over uncleanness
Mark's account of the woman with a discharge of blood who was healed by touching Jesus' cloak
Luke's account of the woman with a discharge of blood, which connects to the purity law in Leviticus
